paper.title_en: First-Principle Calculation of Collins-Soper Kernel from Quasi-Transverse-Momentum-Dependent Wave Functions
paper.abstract_en: The Collins--Soper (CS) kernel controls the rapidity evolution of transverse-momentum-dependent (TMD) parton distributions, enabling QCD factorization and connecting nucleon-structure data across scales. Its long-distance behavior at large transverse separations $b_\perp$ is still poorly constrained due to model dependence. We present a first-principles lattice QCD determination of the CS kernel at the continuum limit and physical pion mass within the large-momentum effective theory framework. Using $2+1$-flavor ensembles ($a=0.052$--$0.105~\mathrm{fm}$, $m_\pi\approx136$--$320~\mathrm{MeV}$), we compute nonlocal equal-time correlators and extract quasi-TMD wave functions. With systematic improvements---hypercubic smearing, nonperturbative renormalization, and a $b_\perp$-unexpanded matching kernel---we obtain the CS kernel in the continuum, chiral, and infinite-momentum limits up to $b_\perp\sim1~\mathrm{fm}$ with controlled uncertainties. The results match perturbative QCD at small $b_\perp$, agree with global phenomenological extractions, and can be incorporated into global fits, providing the most precise lattice constraint on the CS kernel's long-distance behavior for future TMD analyses.
